title: The turnstile and the tip

data.source: Jarzynski (1997), Crooks (1999), Sagawa and Ueda (2010); cited from memory. Simulated thermal rotor of Phoenix_Egg/CORE/MATHEMATICS.md sections IV and VI, seeded.

prediction: Where the potential repeats every half-turn, the log odds of a forward half-turn against a backward one are R6's heat over kT (2 here); for the printed potential that holds only over whole turns; and the work at the cut has no spread and does not obey Jarzynski's equality, because the switch is triggered by a reading of the position.
baseline: The fluctuation theorems: Jarzynski (1997), Crooks (1999); with feedback, Sagawa and Ueda (2010). Decoy: log odds = Q/kT for every potential.
relation: identical for the heat of a whole turn; W_cut is outside the plain work theorem
status_line: CRR here is: saying something the plain work theorem does not cover (W_cut is a switch triggered by a reading, so Jarzynski's equality does not apply); its heat Q, over kT, is a renaming of the fluctuation theorem's log odds for whole turns.
why: With a thermal bath, R6's heat over kT is the logarithm of the odds of a half-turn against its reverse when the potential repeats every half-turn, and of a whole turn in general: that part restates the fluctuation theorem. For the printed potential a forward and a backward half-turn from the hilltop are not a path and its reverse, and the numbers differ. The work at the cut (Phoenix section VI: 'include the event intervention work') had no spread and missed Jarzynski's value, because the theorem needs a schedule that does not look at the system and a cut is a reading. R2 (ASSUMPTION) does not count the backward half-turns the theorem pairs with the forward ones.
